'''Ramón Rogelio Latorre de la Cruz''' (born October 29, 1941) is a Chilean biochemist,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Ram%C3%B3n+Latorre&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C44&as_sdtp= |title=Ramón Latorre |accessdate=July 17, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n85374224/ |title=Latorre, Ramon |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=July 17, 2017}}</ref> The winner of Chile's [[National Prize for Natural Sciences (Chile)|National Prize for Natural Sciences]] in 2002,<ref name="Chile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.uchile.cl/portal/presentacion/historia/grandes-figuras/premios-nacionales/ciencias-/6511/ramon-latorre-de-la-cruz |title=Ramón Latorre de la Cruz |publisher=uchile.cl |accessdate=July 17, 2017}}</ref> he has been recognized for his investigations in the field of the ionic channels of cellular membranes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed?cmd=search&term=de+la+Torre+R%5Bau%5D&dispmax=50|title=de la Torre R[au] - PubMed - NCBI|last=pubmeddev|website=www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ramon_Latorre/stats|title=Ramón Latorre|website=ResearchGate}}</ref>

== Biography ==

He studied secondary in the Chilean School Jose Victorino Lastarria. In 1965 he received a biochemist at the School of Chemistry and Pharmacy. In 1969 he received a doctorate in Sciences with a Doctorate in Biology at the [[University of Chile]], being one of the first students of that degree. He later received a scholarship from the [[National Institute of Health]] de [[EE.UU.]], and finished work in his laboratory of biophysics of this institution until the year 1972. Returned to Chile and held the position in the Faculty of Sciences of assistant professor. After [[1973 Chilean coup d'état]], Returned to the EE.UU. and served in the Department of Physiology at [[Duke University]] as a visiting scientist. Two years later he worked in the Department of Physiological and Pharmacological Sciences of the [[University of Chicago]] as an assistant professor and in 1977 he began to perform his teaching task at the School of Medicine of the [[University of Harvard]].<ref name="Chile"/><ref name="UV">{{Cite web |url=http://cinv.uv.cl/ramon-latorre-2/?lang=en |title=Ramón Latorre |publisher=uv.cl |accessdate=July 17, 2017}}</ref>

Returning to his country (Chile), in 1983 he worked in the Faculty of Sciences of the [[University of Chile]] as professor of Cellular Physiology. The following year he founded with the physicist [[Claudio Teitelboim]] the [[Centro de Estudios Científicos|Center for Scientific Studies of Santiago]], Who later moved to [[Valdivia]].<ref name="Chile"/><ref name="UV"/>
